description: self-fix.sh's hung-fixer kill path (lines 24-26: `tmux -S "$SOCK" kill-session -t "$SESSION" ...; pkill -f "claude --name $SESSION" ...`) terminates the tmux pane and any process whose argv literally contains the string 'claude --name <SESSION>', but does not kill a process group and cannot reach detached grandchild processes the fixer's own claude session may have spawned during up to 45 minutes of autonomous work (e.g. a background curl/python helper it started with & , an additional nested tmux session it created itself while debugging, or a self/issue-dev invocation per its own TASK text step 6). tmux kill-session sends SIGHUP to the pane's foreground process; children that double-fork, ignore SIGHUP, or were started detached will be orphaned. Combined with FIND-023's kill-and-respawn churn, every forced restart is a potential additional orphan-leak point, not just a single one-time risk.
